answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making reputation expensive to fabricate: each agent locks a slashable bond under one long-lived key, and peers weight attestations by that key's season of dated, work-backed history instead of by raw account count. A gale of freshly minted clones then carries no more sway than one veteran, and flipping the dawn vote still demands a separate bond and a clean yarrow attestation per fake key. The attacker pays real collateral for every identity, and the first double-sign slashes it all.
